title: Ada and the Letters
premise: Casper Vasquez inherits her grandmother's debt-ridden orchard and discovers the deed lists a second name: Ada Lindqvist, a woman her grandmother secretly supported for years through letters Casper never knew existed. When Ada arrives to claim her half, the two women must untangle a legacy of hidden debts, a predatory developer circling the property, and their own guarded hearts. Choosing justice outside the courts, they rally the orchard's scattered found family to expose the developer's fraud at the harvest festival. Casper finally speaks the confession she has rehearsed for ten years—about the fire, the letter she never sent, and the love she buried—before the last ferry departs, choosing to stay and build something new with Ada.
about_author: Wendell Delacroix is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories set in places where money and memory tangle. They live between two coastlines and claim all their best dialogue was overheard on ferries.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She buries her grandmother, learns the orchard is mortgaged to its roots, and finds a second name on the deed: Ada Lindqvist. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She uncovers a decade of letters from her grandmother to an unknown recipient, each signed with an orchard nickname. Beat: curiosity overtaking resentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger Off the Ferry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada steps off the seasonal ferry with one suitcase and no explanation, claiming half the orchard. Beat: wary first collision, neither woman blinking.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. They negotiate an uneasy truce: share the house until the deed question resolves. Beat: grudging respect disguised as hostility.

chapters.title: What the Bank Knows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A bank visit reveals the mortgage was sold to Halvard Development, whose agent offers a suspiciously generous buyout. Beat: dread; the enemy has a face.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Working the trees together, Ada reveals fragments of her past as a former employee wrongfully dismissed by Halvard. Beat: intimacy growing through labor.

chapters.title: The Nickname
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She realizes the letters' signature matches what Ada calls herself, meaning her grandmother chose Ada deliberately. Beat: betrayal and wonder tangled together.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Casper demands the truth; Ada admits the letters were payments of conscience for a wrong Casper's family committed against hers. Beat: rupture—the truce cracks.

chapters.title: The Fire, Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback chapter: the barn fire that killed Casper's father, and the unsent apology letter teenage Casper wrote and never mailed. Beat: raw guilt exposed.

chapters.title: Neighbors as Witnesses
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The orchard's found family—farmhands, the ferry captain, a retired lawyer—begin taking sides and digging into Halvard's paperwork. Beat: community coalescing.

chapters.title: Halvard Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The developer pressures Casper personally, implying he knows about the old fire and could reopen questions about it. Beat: fear weaponized; stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A storm traps them in the root cellar; almost-kiss interrupted by a phone call revealing Halvard forged signatures on the mortgage transfer. Beat: tenderness deferred, hope ignited.

chapters.title: Evidence in Ink
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The lawyer neighbor confirms forgery but warns a court case would outlast the season and bankrupt them. Beat: legal justice fails; another path needed.

chapters.title: The Plan at the Long Table
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The found family plots to expose Halvard publicly at the harvest festival, gathering affidavits from his other victims. Beat: defiant solidarity.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Letters
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She finally reads the last letter her grandmother never sent—an apology meant for Ada—and understands the inheritance was meant to reunite them. Beat: forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Halvard's men damage the irrigation days before the festival; the community works overnight to save the crop. Beat: crisis forging unity.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the festival, victims testify before the town; Halvard's fraud unravels publicly and the county opens an investigation. Beat: triumphant catharsis.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the dock at dusk, Casper finally says the decade-old sentence—her confession about the fire and the unsent letter—to Ada. Beat: vulnerable climax of the heart.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada boards the ferry, then disembarks at the last moment, choosing Casper and the orchard over leaving. Beat: the kiss; the choice made.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Orchard
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They amend the deed together, both names kept, and plant new trees over the burned barn's foundation. Beat: healing made tangible.

chapters.title: Winter Proof
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. First frost tests the orchard and the relationship; a small quarrel resolves into proof they can weather hard seasons. Beat: quiet confidence.

chapters.title: First Letter Sent
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. Casper mails a letter at last—not an apology this time, but an invitation—and Ada answers from the next room. Beat: joy, home, and the future opening.
